lines: Pick a class and ride it. Telo Ride now has the class ride screen, driving the bike through the plan.
The header names the class and the mode, with the clock as a timer: seven minutes of thirty.
The segment card counts down the part you're in: its kind, its time left, its progress, and the whole plan.
Power reads against the segment's target. Within ten percent it's on target; otherwise it shows the gap.
The stepper shows the resistance the bike reports, or a dash. Plus and minus nudge it, and switch off when the bike is away.
At each boundary the next level goes to the bike. After a long gap, only the current level is sent.
The class comes from the catalogue: one request, and the ride starts the moment it arrives.
The first HTTP client costs about five kilobytes on the wire, so the bundle budget makes room for it.
Still to come: the video in sync in 5.3, pause, leave or finish in 5.4, and the catalogue API in 6.1.
On a phone the panel stacks in two columns. From tablet width, it's one row of four.
What the tests prove: four new specs drive the screen on a fake clock and a fake bike, and every check is green.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
